name: count
does: exact line (wc -l), non-empty line, word and byte counts

name: find-files
does: find files by name, case-insensitive glob, skipping build/.git folders

name: find-def
does: where a class/struct/enum/function/macro/alias is defined or declared

name: call-sites
does: every use of a symbol, grouped by file, without its definitions and comments

name: diff-files
does: byte-for-byte compare (sha1), whitespace-only check, unified diff; also directories

name: xml-check
does: XML well-formedness with xmllint

name: changed-files
does: uncommitted changes in a git repo (read-only: status + diff --stat)

name: repo-state
does: where a git repo stands: branch, HEAD, upstream, uncommitted changes, submodules with their own changes, whether a commit is in the history (submodules too); --diff adds the full diff including submodules; --log N the last N commit subjects, to match their style

name: route
does: which lead the routing rules would pick for a ticket

name: library-check
does: duplicate notes and file:line references that no longer match the code

name: weekly-report
does: a team's week in numbers: tickets, costs, ratings, staff, problems

name: choose-model
does: the expected-value model's pick of model and effort for a task, with the full table

name: jev
does: ask Jev (TypeSafe router via OpenRouter) which model and effort fit a task

name: skills-scan
does: every Claude Code and office skill: type, size in tokens, uses, pinned model

name: suggest-routines
does: jobs done by hand 3+ times and repeated corrections, as routine/memory suggestions

name: cache-report
does: cold prompt-cache reloads in your chats and whether keep-warm pings would pay

name: workspace-map
does: draft the CLAUDE.md map and department routers (writes only a proposal), or list images without descriptions

name: artifacts-index
does: rebuild the artifacts inbox page, newest first, searchable

name: token-usage
does: where Claude Code tokens went: by kind, source, project, model, day; what fills the context (tool results carried per call); biggest results; costliest sessions

name: usage-index
does: every model call on this machine with exact token counts, attributed to you, agent, team, job, project, model; context breakdown per call

name: routing-report
does: how model picks turned out: Jev vs EV vs overrides vs pins — done rate, cost, time, ratings, sent back, retried

name: arms-selftest
does: tests ARMS approvals (memory map, skills, status line, keep-warm), keep-warm pings and Recos setup in a throwaway HOME; proves real ~/.claude is untouched

name: show
does: line ranges from one or more files with line numbers (instead of several sed -n or whole-file reads)

name: outline
does: classes, functions, methods and headings with line numbers, to find what to read (py, js/ts, c/c++, java/kotlin, go, rust, md, sh)

name: search
does: code search grouped by file, several folders at once; never reads media/binary files or files over 5 MB, so huge repos take seconds (use instead of grep -r)

name: project-info
does: what a project is and how to install, build, test and run it (detected from its files), plus commands that worked in earlier jobs and its handoff

name: sqlite
does: read-only SQLite: tables with row counts and columns, or a query's rows as a table

name: web-shot
does: screenshot of a web page or local HTML with headless Chrome (then Read the PNG to look at it)

name: job-cost
does: where a job's usage went: per agent and model, cache reads/writes/output, context size, what filled it, and where to save

name: handoff-facts
does: facts for save_project_handoff: jobs, files changed, commands and results, questions and answers, costs, commands that worked

name: ui-check
does: after any change to the Agentic OS window: clicks through every app, menu, Preferences and job state in a throwaway copy (fake agents, nothing spent) and lists JS errors, dead buttons, off-screen buttons and overflowing layouts, with screenshots (about 45 s)

name: api-check
does: after any change to the Agentic OS server: exercises its API in a throwaway copy (fake agents, nothing spent) — jobs, follow-ups, recall, commands and the block list, plans, handoffs, skills, settings, restart, a fresh clone — and lists what broke (about 5 s)

name: prompt-size
does: how many tokens each role's fixed instructions and office tools take (what every call re-sends), by section

name: agent-eval
does: after changing agent instructions: real agents on a cheap model in a throwaway office, checking they read in parts, use scripts, refuse to commit, propose plans and save handoffs (a few cents)
